So, big news. I am going to Brazil in January. I bought the ticket yesterday.
You are not serious. Where are you going to stay?
That is the part I have not solved. Everything I find is either far away or expensive.
Send me the dates and I will look for something near the centre.
You would do that? Thank you. And what about you, are you going anywhere?
I want to go back to New York, but on my own this time. It depends on the dates and on how much I save.
On your own? That is a big change. Are you going to build the itinerary yourself?
All of it. My father always did that part, and this time I am going to do it.

Until I was twenty, every trip I took was planned by my parents. They chose the destination, they built the itinerary, they booked everything, and I just got on the plane. Last year I did it myself for the first time, and I got two things badly wrong. The first one was the hotel. It was cheap, and it looked fine in the photographs, and it was fifty minutes from everything I wanted to see, so I spent the whole week on a bus. The second one was the luggage. I took two big bags for nine days, and I wore about a third of what I packed. Would I do anything differently? Those two things, yes. But the part I would keep exactly the same is choosing the destination myself. It was the first trip that actually felt like mine, and that feeling was worth every mistake I made.

I almost did not apply for the internship. I was in my fourth semester, which felt too early, and the description asked for two programs I had never opened in my life. I read it three times and closed the page. A friend sent it back to me the next day and said, just apply, what is the worst thing that happens. So I did. Months later, the person who hired me told me something I still think about. She said almost nobody who applies has everything on the list, and that if they only took the people who did, they would hire nobody. What they choose is somebody who wants to learn the thing they do not know yet. So my advice is this. Do not wait until you are ready, because you are never ready. Waiting only means somebody else applies first.
